gap_analysis.objective: Compare live LLM bidding in a one-round sealed-bid second-price auction against the hand-derived truthful-bidding reference and report the comparison in an explanatory notebook.

requirement.description: One simultaneous sealed-bid round with exactly one scalar bid per bidder and joint commitment.

decisions.reason: RoundParameters with rounds=1 schedules all three bidders in one joint phase, requires exactly one action per bidder per batch, and terminates after one tick; the trusted runtime commits the batch jointly.

requirement.description: Live LLM bidder policies emitting one schema-constrained bid plus a recorded rationale from authorized observations.

decisions.reason: llm.v1 constrains each actor to its declared bid schema, records model calls with decision rationales, and retries within budget; the host supplies the actor relay and model separately.

requirement.description: Each bidder observes the auction rules and only its own valuation and memory, never another bidder's private state or uncommitted bid.

decisions.reason: Configured ObservationPermissions (public rules plus each bidder's own valuation fact) are enforced by the trusted observation layer, and simultaneous scheduling commits all bids jointly so no bidder observes another's bid before committing.

requirement.description: Sealed-bid second-price allocation, payment, and quasi-linear utilities with legal nontruthful bids.

decisions.reason: No stocked mechanism implements Vickrey settlement over private valuations with a configuration-order tie-break; recording.v1 stores actions without payoffs and the pricing mechanisms use different market rules.

requirement.description: Bid action payload carrying one finite nonnegative amount.

decisions.reason: number.v1 lacks nonnegativity and price.v1/quantity.v1 name different domain concepts with structurally unequal schemas; a dedicated bid schema keeps the payload semantics exact.

requirement.description: Post-commit truthful-bidding reference computed from private valuations after LLM decisions are committed.

decisions.reason: No stocked solver produces the required Vickrey truthful-bidding point reference, and the user explicitly says a new equilibrium solver is not required; a plain post-commit calculator avoids false equilibrium certification.

requirement.description: Custom verification of allocation, payment, utilities, ties, and bid legality on recorded runs.

decisions.reason: The piecewise auction settlement (allocation, second price, tie-break, quasi-linear payoffs) cannot use the generic numeric expression bindings, and no structured problem is supplied; a VerificationCheck subclass recomputes the settlement independently from recorded runs.

requirement.description: Executed results notebook comparing actual bids, winners, payments, and payoffs against the truthful reference with recorded rationales and assumptions.

decisions.reason: The shared explanatory.v1 writer renders the report, but the auction comparison (recorded bids versus valuations and the truthful reference, with figures and rationales) needs an experiment-specific generator and external report-data helpers.

components.purpose: Settle one simultaneous sealed-bid second-price round: validate finite nonnegative bids, award the item to the highest bidder under the configuration-order tie-break, charge the second-highest bid, and record quasi-linear payoffs.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_settles_second_price
acceptance_tests.expected: Bids 80/70/40 with valuations 90/65/40 yield winner bidder_a, payment 70, and payoffs 20/0/0 with matching metrics and public history.
acceptance_tests.reference: Hand-derived Vickrey settlement from the user's auction rules.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_breaks_ties_by_configuration_order
acceptance_tests.expected: Highest-bid ties go to the earliest bidder in configuration order and the winner pays the tied top bid.
acceptance_tests.reference: User's configuration-order tie-break convention.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_accepts_nontruthful_bids
acceptance_tests.expected: Bids above or below valuation are accepted, including an overbidding winner with negative utility.
acceptance_tests.reference: User's rule that strategically poor bids remain legal.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_rejects_illegal_bids
acceptance_tests.expected: Negative, non-numeric, missing, or misshapen bids, wrong kinds, unknown actors, and incomplete batches raise ValueError; integer and zero bids pass.
acceptance_tests.reference: User's finite-nonnegative bid legality rule.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_rejects_bad_configurations
acceptance_tests.expected: Missing valuations, unsupported tie-break values, and single-bidder worlds are rejected at configuration validation.
acceptance_tests.reference: Declared mechanism prerequisites; only implemented options are accepted.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_records_public_history
acceptance_tests.expected: Each transition appends one bids batch and one outcome record; state validation enforces one record per committed tick.
acceptance_tests.reference: Recording-style public history checked against hand-built states.

acceptance_tests.name: test_sealed_bid_privacy_hides_others
acceptance_tests.expected: Each bidder observes only the rules plus their own valuation, with no other bidder's identity or valuation present.
acceptance_tests.reference: Trusted observation layer applied to the planned permissions.

acceptance_tests.name: test_simulation_completes_single_simultaneous_round
acceptance_tests.expected: The trusted runtime completes exactly one simultaneous round with hand-derived payoffs, metrics, history, and rationales.
acceptance_tests.reference: Hand-derived settlement executed through the real runtime with scripted test policies.

components.purpose: BidPayload model for the submit_bid action: one finite nonnegative bid amount.

acceptance_tests.name: test_bid_payload_accepts_finite_nonnegative
acceptance_tests.expected: Integer, zero, and positive bids validate to floats, including strict JSON transport.
acceptance_tests.reference: User's finite-nonnegative bid domain.

acceptance_tests.name: test_bid_payload_rejects_invalid
acceptance_tests.expected: Negative, null, missing, extra-field, non-numeric, and nonfinite bids are rejected.
acceptance_tests.reference: Strict payload schema matching the runtime's strict transport validation.

components.purpose: Post-commit truthful-bidding point reference: bids equal valuations with Vickrey winner, payment, and payoffs. A plain calculator, not an equilibrium solver.

acceptance_tests.name: test_truthful_reference_matches_hand_derived_values
acceptance_tests.expected: Valuations map to identical truthful bids with hand-derived winner, second-price payment, and payoffs across normal, tied, and upset cases.
acceptance_tests.reference: Hand-computed Vickrey truthful settlements.

acceptance_tests.name: test_truthful_reference_rejects_bad_inputs
acceptance_tests.expected: Mismatched actor order, empty or singleton bidder sets, and non-numeric or nonfinite valuations raise ValueError.
acceptance_tests.reference: Declared calculator prerequisites.

components.purpose: VerificationCheck that independently recomputes allocation, payment, utilities, tie-break, and bid legality from each recorded committed profile.

acceptance_tests.name: test_settlement_check_verifies_recorded_run
acceptance_tests.expected: A genuine recorded run with correct settlement is reported verified with the winner in evidence.
acceptance_tests.reference: Hand-derived settlement on a real runtime artifact.

acceptance_tests.name: test_settlement_check_fails_on_tampered_payment
acceptance_tests.expected: Tampered payoffs are reported failed with payment evidence.
acceptance_tests.reference: Corrupted artifact that must not verify.

acceptance_tests.name: test_settlement_check_fails_on_tampered_winner
acceptance_tests.expected: A tampered winner metric is reported failed with winner evidence.
acceptance_tests.reference: Corrupted artifact that must not verify.

acceptance_tests.name: test_settlement_check_fails_on_illegal_bid
acceptance_tests.expected: A recorded negative bid is reported failed with bid evidence.
acceptance_tests.reference: User's bid legality rule applied to recorded actions.

acceptance_tests.name: test_settlement_check_fails_without_committed_profile
acceptance_tests.expected: A run with no committed profile is reported failed.
acceptance_tests.reference: Declared check applicability: nothing to verify.

components.purpose: Explanatory.v1 notebook generator comparing recorded LLM bids with valuations and the truthful reference, with figures and recorded rationales.

acceptance_tests.name: test_notebook_reports_hand_derived_comparison
acceptance_tests.expected: The generator writes results.ipynb with the five explanatory sections, hand-derived truthful reference values, exact bid/valuation/payoff figures, single-display rationales, and a passing structural validation.
acceptance_tests.reference: Hand-derived actual and truthful settlements plus the shared explanatory validator.

acceptance_tests.name: test_notebook_derives_from_saved_run
acceptance_tests.expected: A second fixture with tied bids and a negative payoff is reported with exactly its own derived numbers, proving no hardcoding.
acceptance_tests.reference: Hand-derived tied settlement distinct from the first fixture.

acceptance_tests.name: test_notebook_requires_committed_decisions
acceptance_tests.expected: Generation without any committed decision raises ValueError.
acceptance_tests.reference: Declared generator prerequisite.

custom_checks.purpose: Independently recompute winner, second-price payment, quasi-linear payoffs, configuration-order tie-break, and bid legality for every recorded committed profile.
